summary: Karel Werner (1925–2019) worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at Masaryk University and Palacký University Olomouc under Vincenc Lesný and others. His career included posts at Durham University (1969–1990) and Masaryk University (1993–1998).

Karen Christina Lang specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at Banaras Hindu University, the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives, and the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, later serving as professor at the University of Virginia.

Karen Katsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. She held posts as a part-time lecturer at Hanazono University (attested 2006) and as a lecturer at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Karen McCarthy Brown (1942–2015) was a scholar of religion. She studied at Smith College, Union Theological Seminary, and Temple University. She served for many years as professor of anthropology at Drew University (ca. 1976–2009).
Karen Nelson Villanueva works in religious studies. She earned her PhD at the California Institute of Integral Studies and pursued traditional studies under Geshe Ngawang Dakpa and Lobsang Chökyi.
Karen Nero has held academic posts at the University of Canterbury and the University of Otago, where she taught Sally McAra.

Karen O'Brien-Kop works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She earned her PhD from SOAS University of London and held lecturing posts at the University of Roehampton (attested 2020) and King's College London (attested 2026).

Karin Meyers specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under Jay L. Garfield and served as assistant professor and director of the Buddhist studies MA program at Kathmandu University's Centre for Buddhist Studies at Rangjung Yeshe Institute.

Karin Preisendanz (born 1958) is an Indologist and philosopher educated at the University of Hamburg. Her career includes posts at the University of British Columbia (1990–1993), University of Hamburg (1993–1999), and University of Vienna (from 1999).

Karl Albert Agathon Benary (1807–1860) was a linguist who studied at Göttingen and Halle-Wittenberg, and under Franz Bopp. He served as a professor at Köllnisches Gymnasium (1833–1860) and Privatdozent at Humboldt University of Berlin (1839).

Karl Ammer (1911–1970) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Vienna (ca. 1929–1934). He served as Director of the Institute of Indology at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg from ca. 1955 to 1970.

Karl Benedikt Hase (1780–1864) worked in linguistics and history. After studying at Helmstedt and Jena, he held long-term posts at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes, and the Faculty of Arts of Paris.

Karl Brugmann (1849–1919) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Georg Curtius at Halle and Leipzig. After serving as ordinarius at Freiburg (1884), he held a professorship in Indo-European linguistics at Leipzig from 1887 to 1919.

Karl Brunnhölzl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Khenpo Lama Thubten.

Karl Debreczeny specializes in Tibetology and art history. He earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Hung Wu and Jenny Purtle, and later served as a curator at the Rubin Museum of Art (attested 2008).

Karl Eduard Zachariae von Lingenthal (1812–1894) was a legal historian. He studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and subsequently held an academic post at Heidelberg University from ca. 1836 to 1842.
Karl Eugen Neumann (1865–1915) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Leipzig and completed his doctoral work under Richard Pischel between ca. 1888 and 1891.
Karl Felix Halm (1809–1882) was a scholar in linguistics and history. From ca. 1856 to 1882, he held dual posts at the University of Munich and the Bavarian State Library.
Karl Ferdinand Johansson (1860–1926) was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at Uppsala University starting in 1880 and later served as professor there from ca. 1893 to 1925.

Karl Florenz (1865–1939) was a Japanologist and linguist who studied at Leipzig under Ernst Windisch. He taught at the University of Tokyo (1889–1917) before holding professorships at the Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut and the University of Hamburg (ca. 1914–1935).
